why: Sorting each part independently gives a sorted whole exactly when everything on the left is <= everything on the right, i.e. max(left) <= min(right). So for every cut you need a prefix maximum and a suffix minimum, both precomputed in one pass each; the sorting in the story is never actually done.
hints: After sorting both parts, where can the array still be out of order? Only at the join.
The join is fine iff the largest left element is <= the smallest right element. So a cut after index i is valid iff prefixMax[i] <= suffixMin[i+1].
Build suffixMin right to left, then scan left to right with a running max and count valid cuts. O(N) time, O(N) space.
pitfalls: Both parts must be non-empty: there are N-1 cuts, not N+1.
Equal values are fine (non-decreasing): use <=, as in [5,5,5] giving 2.
Actually sorting each split is O(N^2 log N) and times out at N = 100000.
